## Circular to Licensed Corporations Substantial Shareholders

This circular is to bring to the attention of licensed corporations of the provisions pertaining to  substantial  shareholders  under  the  Securities  and  Futures  Ordinance  ('SFO')  and  the related transitional arrangements.

Pursuant  to  section  131(1)  of  the  SFO,  a  person  shall  not  become  or  continue  to  be  a substantial  shareholder  of  a  licensed  corporation  without  first  being  approved  by  the Securities and Futures Commission ('SFC').  Under section 6 of Schedule 1 to the SFO, a reference  to  a  substantial  shareholder  includes  the  person  concerned  and  any  of  his associates.

Please  note  that  the  new  definition  of  'associate'  is  wider  than  that  under  the  repealed Securities  and  Futures  Commission Ordinance or Leveraged Foreign Exchange Ordinance. In  particular,  as  stipulated  in  paragraph  ( l )  of  the  definition  in  Part  1  of  Schedule  1  to  the SFO, 'associate', in relation to a person, means - in  circumstances concerning the securities of or other interest in a corporation, or rights arising out of the holding of such securities or such interest, any other person with whom the person has an agreement or arrangement -

- (i) with respect to the acquisition, holding or disposal of such securities or such interest; or
- (ii) under which they undertake to act together in exercising their voting power at general meetings of the corporations.

The now wider definition of 'associate' renders certain persons, who were not regarded as substantial shareholders under the former regime, to become so by operation of the new law. A person, being aware that he falls to be a substantial shareholder under such circumstances should as soon as reasonable practicable and in any event within 3 business days after he became so aware, apply to the SFC for approval to continue to be a substantial shareholder of the  corporation.    Pending  the  approval  of  the  SFC,  he  may  continue  to  enjoy  his  rights  as substantial shareholder.

Separately, as transitional arrangements to the new regime, section 58 of Schedule 10 to the SFO provides that where approval to be a substantial shareholder has been given by the SFC under section 26A of the repealed Securities and Futures Commission Ordinance or section 14A  of  the  repealed  Leveraged  Foreign  Exchange  Trading  Ordinance,  and  the  approval subsists  immediately  before  the  commencement  of  Part  V  of  the  SFO,  the  approval  shall, upon such commencement, be deemed to have been granted under section 132 of the SFO.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

In relation to the above transitional provisions, the SFC received enquiries on whether certain substantial shareholders of a licensed corporation, who have been subsisting since the first grant  of  the  corporation's  registration  or  licence  under  the  former  regime,  are  required  to apply to the SFC for continuing to be substantial shareholders of that corporation under the SFO.    On  this  matter,  the  SFC  takes  the  view  that  persons  approved  as  substantial shareholders, by virtue of their being disclosed to the SFC as being substantial shareholders at the point of approval of registration or licence of a corporation under the former regime, in addition  to  persons  who  were  expressly  approved  as  substantial  shareholders  of  the corporation  under  the  relevant  repealed  provisions,  are  not  required  to  seek  the  SFC's approval to continue to be substantial shareholders of such corporation under section 132 of the SFO.

Should you have any queries on the above, please contact your responsible Intermediaries Relationship Manager of the Licensing Department.

Licensing Department Intermediaries and Investment Products Division Securities and Futures Commission
